shots.prompt: Slow crane shot descending over a joyful Greek wedding at dusk: dancers circling, torches flickering, garlands swaying, a lyre and double pipes playing, children weaving between tables. Warm golden light, lively festive music.

lines.text: My name is Mikon. I sell salt fish at the harbour in Corinth.

shots.prompt: At the courtyard gate, Mikon arrives beaming, chest puffed with pride, hugging a wicker basket of salt fish like treasure. He waves at someone off screen. Medium shot, warm torchlight.

lines.text: Tonight my cousin Thea is getting married, and I've brought the best I've got.

shots.prompt: Lykon stands at a long table and waves Mikon over, grinning. As Mikon arrives, Lykon's nose wrinkles; he leans toward the basket and sniffs, horrified.

lines.text: Mikon! Over here, I saved you a seat. Wait. Is that fish?

shots.prompt: Two-shot at the table. Lykon stares at the basket in disbelief. Mikon lifts it proudly like a prize.

lines.text: You brought fish to a wedding?
Salt fish from Lechaion. The good kind. It's a present.

shots.prompt: Aunt Kleio swoops in, snatches the basket out of Mikon's hands and holds it at arm's length, then pushes him firmly down onto the bench and puts a cup of wine in his hand.

lines.text: Give that to me before the bride smells it. Sit down, Mikon, and enjoy yourself for once.

shots.prompt: Uncle Demeas climbs onto a bench, wine cup raised, and bangs the table for silence. The guests groan and laugh. Low angle, comic.

lines.text: Friends! Friends, quiet, please. I'll be brief. I won't be brief.

shots.prompt: Demeas toasts the couple with huge gestures, spilling wine. Cut-in: the bride Thea and the groom Nikias at the head table laugh, embarrassed, and the crowd cheers and throws petals.

lines.text: To Thea and Nikias! May you have more children than this family has goats!

shots.prompt: Kleio, arms folded, glares up at Demeas. Demeas, wobbling on the bench, answers with wounded dignity.

lines.text: Demeas, sit down before you fall into the lamb again.
That was one time, Kleio, and the lamb started it.

shots.prompt: Mikon, delighted with himself, pops a green olive into his mouth, leans close to Lykon and nudges him, eyes twinkling with a joke he can't wait to tell.

lines.text: Lykon. Lykon. Have you heard the one about the goat who wandered into the temple of Zeus?

shots.prompt: Close-up on Lykon, pained, pleading, hands pressed together.

lines.text: Mikon, it's your cousin's wedding. Not the goat one. Anything but the goat one.

shots.prompt: Mikon tells the joke with big theatrical gestures, acting out the goat and the priest, the olive bulging in his cheek, guests nearby starting to listen.

lines.text: So the goat walks up to the altar, and the priest looks at the goat, and the goat looks at the priest...

shots.prompt: Mikon bursts out laughing at his own joke, throws his head back, inhales sharply mid-laugh, and freezes. His eyes go wide. He clutches his throat. Comic timing turning to alarm.

lines.text: Ha! No, wait, wait, this is the good part, this is the...

shots.prompt: Lykon turns, puzzled, then worried, as Mikon turns red and silently waves his arms, unable to breathe.

lines.text: Mikon? Mikon, are you all right? You've gone a very strange colour.

shots.prompt: Chaos at the table: Kleio leaps up shouting and points; Demeas thumps Mikon's back far too gently; cups topple.

lines.text: He's choking! Somebody hit him on the back! Not like that, Demeas, harder!

shots.prompt: The groom Nikias grabs Mikon from behind and squeezes; the bride Thea, in her gold gown, rushes in, frightened and furious.

lines.text: I've got him, I've got him! Breathe, cousin, just breathe!
Mikon, don't you dare. Not today!

shots.prompt: Point of view from the ground looking up: Kleio, Thea and Lykon lean over the camera under the vine-covered pergola, frightened faces haloed by torchlight. The image slowly blurs and darkens and the sounds of the party muffle and fade.

lines.text: Mikon? Mikon, look at me. Stay with us.

shots.prompt: The torchlight blurs into soft glowing circles and fades almost to black. Muffled heartbeat.

lines.text: One moment I was laughing. The next, everyone I loved was leaning over me, and their voices were getting very far away.

shots.prompt: The next night, the same courtyard cleared and quiet, lit by candles. Mikon lies on a table under a white sheet with flowers. The family stands around him. Kleio looks up suddenly; Demeas blinks.

lines.text: Did anybody put the coin in his mouth? For the ferryman?
I thought you did.

shots.prompt: Kleio throws up her hands. Demeas eyes the platter of lamb, sheepish and sad.

lines.text: I was doing the lamb!
Well, the lamb's going cold now. He'd want us to eat.

shots.prompt: Close-up of Thea, still in her gold gown, eyes wet, a small sad laugh.

lines.text: He never even finished the joke. I wanted to know what the priest said.

shots.prompt: Slow rising shot above the candlelit table and the family, the camera drifting up into the dark night sky.

lines.text: Nobody put a coin under my tongue for the ferryman. They were grieving, and nobody thought of it.

shots.prompt: Mikon wakes on a stone bench beside the glowing river, sits up groggily, blinks, and stares at the river in growing alarm.

lines.text: Oh. Oh, no. Is that a river? Why is it glowing?

shots.prompt: Hermes crouches beside Mikon with a kind, amused smile and steadies him with a hand on his shoulder.

lines.text: Easy. Easy, sit up slowly. You'll feel cold for a while. That passes.
The wedding. I was at the wedding.

shots.prompt: Close on Hermes, gentle, honest, a little sorry.

lines.text: You were. And then you laughed with an olive in your mouth. I'm sorry, Mikon. You died.

shots.prompt: Mikon, stunned, covers his face. Hermes shrugs, trying to cheer him up.

lines.text: I died. At a wedding. In front of everyone.
If it helps, most of them were looking at the lamb.

shots.prompt: Hermes points down the long dock to Charon, who stands in a black boat in the mist and slowly turns his glowing eyes toward them.

lines.text: That's Charon. He takes one coin from every passenger. Without one, you wait on this bank. A hundred years.

shots.prompt: Mikon's face falls. Hermes leans in with a mischievous wink.

lines.text: A hundred years.
Unless you find a coin.

shots.prompt: Huge pull-back crane shot: Mikon tiny on his bench, the glowing river, the dock, the endless colonnade and thousands of faint drifting souls.

lines.text: Everyone you've ever heard of came through here. Heroes, kings, a man with a lyre.

shots.prompt: The camera keeps rising into the dark until the river is a thin glowing thread, then holds.

lines.text: Nobody wrote down the people who were already waiting. This is the story of one of them.
